text:
A: Hiya, love! Ooh, are you the one with the lilac bedroom? I'm Nicola.
B: Hiya, yeah, that's me. I'm Ffion. Sorry, it's a bit messy behind me.
A: Don't be daft, you should see my kitchen. Where are you then?
B: Wrexham, in North Wales.
A: Oh, lovely. I'm Eltham, South East London. So what are you up to? Are you at uni? I saw the hoodie.
B: Yeah, final year, occupational therapy. I'm on placement at the moment, on an older adults' ward.
A: Oh, are you? That's lovely. What does that involve then, day to day? I'm honestly asking, I've never really known what an OT does.
B: Erm, so it's sort of helping people manage everyday things again. Like if someone's had a fall, we'll see if they can get in and out of bed safely, or make a cup of tea in the kitchen, and then what they'd need at home, like rails or a perching stool. It's kind of about keeping people independent, really. I don't know if that makes sense.
A: No, that makes perfect sense. My mum's had an OT come out, actually. They put a rail in by her front step. Made a real difference.
B: Oh, that's good. That's the bit I like, when you can see it actually helps.
A: And do you like the older patients? Some people find it hard.
B: I love them, honestly. They tell you all their stories. One lady yesterday told me about dancing in Rhyl in the fifties, she was so funny.
A: Oh, bless her. You've got a kind face for it, I said that about your photo. You remind me of my daughter Jess when she was at uni.
B: Aw, that's really nice. Is she older now?
A: Twenty-seven! Don't. Lives in Dartford with her partner. And my son Ryan's up in Manchester, so I don't see him as much as I'd like. Do you want to stay near home when you finish?
B: Yeah, definitely. I'd like a job with the health board near Wrexham. I tried Liverpool for a bit and, erm, it wasn't for me.
A: Nothing wrong with that, love. Ryan was the opposite, couldn't get away quick enough. Different people, aren't they?
B: Yeah. My mum's a pharmacist at the hospital, so it'd be nice to be near her.
A: Oh, that's handy, you'll be in the same building. Do you get any time off with all that?
B: Not really, I work in a café on Saturdays as well, in the kitchen, so I'm shattered by Saturday night. I just have my tea and watch Gavin & Stacey.
A: Oh, Gavin & Stacey, I love it. Who's your favourite?
B: Nessa, obviously.
A: Obviously! "What's occurring." Sorry, that was a terrible Welsh accent, you're allowed to tell me off.
B: No, it was alright! Better than my brother's.
A: Ha! Have you got a dog? I've got Murphy, he's under the table, he's always under the table.
B: Bonnie, she's a Jack Russell. She's going a bit deaf, so she doesn't come when I call her anyway.
A: Oh, Murphy's selectively deaf. Hears a crisp packet from two rooms away, mind.
B: Bonnie's exactly the same with cheese!
A: They always are. So when do you finish, next summer? Have you got your big exams and all that coming up?
B: Erm, yeah, a few assessments. I get a bit nervous with them, to be honest.
A: Oh, everyone does, love. My Jess used to ring me in a right state, and she always...
